finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the `feed` POST parameter is passed straight to file_get_contents(), which fetches http(s)/ftp URLs (and other stream wrappers). There is no auth check, no scheme or host allowlist, and no block on internal IPs. The response body is not returned, but its length is echoed. That gives a blind SSRF with a size oracle, so an attacker can probe internal hosts and ports, reach cloud metadata endpoints, and tell open services from closed ones by the length or by a false result. Local file:// paths also work, so an attacker can learn file existence and size.

trace.note: Gate is only REQUEST_METHOD === POST and isset($_POST['feed']). require_admin() is not called.
The user-controlled value goes directly into file_get_contents().
strlen($xml) is echoed back, which is the oracle.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() is defined (line 4) but is not called on this branch; it is only used on the set_webhook branch. There is no URL parsing, scheme or host allowlist, or private-IP check. No allow_url_fopen restriction is visible in this file, though it may be set in php.ini.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] straight into file_get_contents() and echoes strlen(); require_admin() (defined at line 4) is only called at line 18 on the set_webhook branch, and no URL, scheme or host validation exists anywhere in the file.
